preamble: Diphthongization of long [ɛː] to [ai] lowers the onset and adds a front off-glide. Icelandic completed it as a phonemic change: Old Norse æ, pronounced [ɛː] in 12th-century Icelandic, is now the diphthong /ai/, still spelled æ. Quebec French shows the same development synchronically: long /ɛː/ in closed syllables is realized anywhere from [ɛɪ̯] to [aɪ̯] depending on the speaker (fête [faɪ̯t]).

examples.note: Old Norse æ [ɛː] became the diphthong /ai/, which the letter æ still represents.
Same development before a consonant cluster, where the diphthong is short and preaspiration precedes the stop.
Long /ɛː/ diphthongizes in closed syllables; outcomes range over [ɛɪ̯], [ei̯], [æɪ̯] and [aɪ̯].
Before /ʁ/ the diphthong has a low onset.
